title: Seishun Buta Yarou wa Santa Claus no Yume wo Minai
content:
You know, for a moment, we actually thought the series was gonna capitalize on the theatrical releases ever since movie one and two dropped, and it was accepted as fact when movie three released, which was not even that long ago. So believe me, Rascal Does Not Dream of Santa Claus being a seasonal TV release was a huge deal for fans.

For once, and from afar, this season felt so much like season one. However, once you zoom in, you’re left at strange places, surrounded by new characters, with the culprit remaining once more familiar. Puberty Syndrome.

Ha, you thought once the main characters escapes highschool they’ll rid themselves, and hopefully the world, from the paranormal activity curse that’s been tearing at them and their loved ones for years, but no, the world is full of insecure teenagers. And Sakuta and folks apparently have all the time and energy to be involved yet again.

This season honestly feels like more of the same old stuff. A cocktail of sort. A remix of the same tired situations, syndromes and drama. At some point you start feeling like you yourself are experiencing a Deja Vu Puberty Syndrome. Apparently this was a trend with the art as well. Maybe we can blame the art style, or perhaps the inability of the artist to draw more than two types of women, long haired and short haired. Toyohama’s dyed hair color was doing some overtime work keeping by designs unique enough. But add one more character and the illusion starts to fade. A few more and you’d seriously have a hard time trying to tell everyone apart.

One other nitpick is the fact that the show tries to shove down non sensical “scientific” explanations to all the weird phenomenons than keep happening. The show is at its best when the characters are facing the phenomenons as metaphorical personifications of their internal struggles without the need of rationalizing them. And even then, this season pales in comparison to what came before. On one hand, the amount of Puberty Syndrome cases presented is respectable. On the other hand, they felt more like background elements with the amount of slice of life-y direction that took place. Slowing the pace down and taking precious time walking through dialogue.

What else could be wrong here, I wonder. Oh right! the Puberty Syndrome cases. How do I say this? The show has officially reached the “goofy” valley with all the Santa Claus cosplay shenanigans. I’m not gonna press too much on any spoilers, but there comes a moment when you are led to believe that Oprah Winfrey herself would to step in and hand out cosplays to every living organisms in Sakuta’s vicinity, looking to drive shock factor as cheaply as possible.

All in all. An average reaction to this season would be on the same wavelength as Sakuta’s monotonic demeanour. Unimpressed but still decent.

Overall: 7.64/10.
